rundown.title: Learn: New exposure, or new visibility?
rundown.subtitle: Why a bigger number is not always worse news

turns.text: Cole, the finding count jumped this week. Should the team panic?
turns.caption: Cole, the finding count jumped this week. Should the team panic?

turns.text: Not yet. First ask where the new findings came from. If they're on machines we've been scanning all along, that's new exposure. Something changed, and it needs a look.
turns.caption: Not yet. First ask where the new findings came from. If they're on machines we've been scanning all along, that's new exposure. Something changed, and it needs a look.

turns.text: But if they're on machines we only just started scanning, or just gave the scanner credentials for, that's new visibility. The risk was already there. We can finally see it.
turns.caption: But if they're on machines we only just started scanning, or just gave the scanner credentials for, that's new visibility. The risk was already there. We can finally see it.

turns.text: So a higher number can actually mean better coverage.
turns.caption: So a higher number can actually mean better coverage.

turns.text: Exactly. And the reverse is the trap. When a finding disappears from a machine that missed its scan, that's not a fix. It's unverified until a rescan proves it.
turns.caption: Exactly. And the reverse is the trap. When a finding disappears from a machine that missed its scan, that's not a fix. It's unverified until a rescan proves it.

turns.text: New exposure, new visibility, verified fixed, unverified. Four different stories, and this station keeps them apart for you.
turns.caption: New exposure, new visibility, verified fixed, unverified. Four different stories, and this station keeps them apart for you.

turns.text: Security news. Here's what CISA flagged this week.
turns.caption: Security news. Here's what CISA flagged this week.

turns.text: Seven vulnerabilities joined the known exploited list in the last seven days.
turns.caption: Seven vulnerabilities joined the known exploited list in the last seven days.

turns.text: On the list: WordPress Core, Ivanti Connect Secure, GitLab Community Edition, Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software, and Broadcom VMware ESX.
turns.caption: On the list: WordPress Core, Ivanti Connect Secure, GitLab Community Edition, Cisco Secure Firewall ASA Software, and Broadcom VMware ESX.

turns.text: Plus one more on screen.
turns.caption: Plus one more on screen.

turns.text: If any of those are in your environment, your exposure desk will call it out.
turns.caption: If any of those are in your environment, your exposure desk will call it out.

turns.text: Cloudflare Zero Wire has five briefings marked needs attention: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free, php2shell, eMudhra certificate compromise, node2shell, and Citrix NetScaler command execution.
turns.caption: Cloudflare Zero Wire has five briefings marked needs attention: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free, php2shell, eMudhra certificate compromise, node2shell, and Citrix NetScaler command execution.

turns.text: Those are public briefings, not findings on our network. Open the news desk for the sources and patch guidance. Matching open findings get context on their action cards.
turns.caption: Those are public briefings, not findings on our network. Open the news desk for the sources and patch guidance. Matching open findings get context on their action cards.

turns.text: Cloudflare coverage is a compensating control. It does not replace the vendor patch or a rescan, and we have not verified coverage for this environment.

zero_wire.title: Linux IPv4 TCP use-after-free
zero_wire.summary: Prioritize patching. Atlas updated its distribution review to report fixed RHEL kernels and remaining vendor-specific patch gaps. Check the running host kernel against your distribution's CVE advisory, apply its fixed kernel, and complete the required reboot or vendor-supported activation procedure. Verify that the fix is active, including on container hosts and Kubernetes nodes.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: Magic Transit customers can use Cloudflare Network Firewall to reduce exposure by filtering IPv4 TCP packets carrying IP options before they reach their infrastructure. Coverage depends on routing and firewall configuration and does not replace kernel patching.

zero_wire.title: php2shell
zero_wire.summary: Prioritize patching. Cloudflare reported that PHP CTF submissions helped harden php2shell WAF protections and create new detections. Patch the PHP runtime using the original security advisory and separately review PHP's session upload progress advisory for CVE-2026-115560. Keep compensating controls in place while patching, and ask managed hosting providers to confirm each issue's status.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: Cloudflare has WAF rules for known php2shell exploit patterns. They are a compensating control, not a fix for the vulnerable PHP runtime. Review your WAF configuration to determine whether you are protected. Paid plans Free plans

zero_wire.title: eMudhra certificate compromise
zero_wire.summary: Review trust settings. Cloudflare published follow-up research on forged certificates, client patching progress, and the limitations of its measurements. Identify systems that rely on the affected certificate chain, update trust stores and client software according to the official response, and review customer-managed origins, mutual TLS, and container images.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: No WAF rules are applicable to this certificate-trust incident.

zero_wire.title: node2shell
zero_wire.summary: Assess your exposure. Cloudflare documented two WAF rules and their default Log action. Identify every Brotli decoder in running runtimes, dependencies, and container images, then use each vendor's security guidance to update or otherwise remove the vulnerable decoder.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: Cloudflare has WAF rules for documented Node2Shell request patterns. They default to Log and customers must configure them to Block if blocking mitigation is needed. Review your WAF configuration to determine whether you are protected. Paid plans

zero_wire.title: Citrix NetScaler command execution
zero_wire.summary: Prioritize patching. Cloudflare published defense-in-depth guidance while distinguishing web authentication from other gateway traffic. Use Citrix's bulletin to identify and update affected appliances. Treat suspected compromise separately from patching, and review exposed gateway services and incident-response guidance.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: Cloudflare has a WAF rule for the documented NetScaler HTTP exploit path. Review your WAF configuration to determine whether you are protected. Paid plans

zero_wire.title: WordPress SQL injection and RCE
zero_wire.summary: Update affected systems. Cloudflare updated its response with vulnerability and remediation guidance. Confirm WordPress update status against the vendor release and patch guidance. Keep any compensating controls in place while remediation is completed.
zero_wire.cloudflare_coverage: Cloudflare has WAF rules for documented WordPress exploit paths. They are a compensating control, not a replacement for updating WordPress. Review your WAF configuration to determine whether you are protected. Paid plans

rundown.title: Learn: EPSS in sixty seconds
rundown.subtitle: What the exploit prediction score does and does not tell you

turns.text: You'll hear us mention EPSS. Cole, what is it, in plain English?
turns.caption: You'll hear us mention EPSS. Cole, what is it, in plain English?

turns.text: It's the Exploit Prediction Scoring System, run by FIRST. Every day it estimates the chance that a vulnerability sees exploitation activity somewhere in the next thirty days.
turns.caption: It's the Exploit Prediction Scoring System, run by FIRST. Every day it estimates the chance that a vulnerability sees exploitation activity somewhere in the next thirty days.

turns.text: So a high score means we're about to get hacked?
turns.caption: So a high score means we're about to get hacked?

turns.text: No, and that's the common mistake. It describes activity across the internet, not the odds that your environment gets breached. It's a signal for ordering work.
turns.caption: No, and that's the common mistake. It describes activity across the internet, not the odds that your environment gets breached. It's a signal for ordering work.

turns.text: Use it alongside CISA's known exploited list, which tells you attacks are already happening, and alongside what the asset actually does for the business.
turns.caption: Use it alongside CISA's known exploited list, which tells you attacks are already happening, and alongside what the asset actually does for the business.

turns.text: Known exploited first, then likely to be exploited, then everything else. That's a plan a small team can actually follow.
turns.caption: Known exploited first, then likely to be exploited, then everything else. That's a plan a small team can actually follow.
